title: 2017 Teacher Assignment, Reporting & Parent Calendar Dashboard
description: I redesigned and rebuilt the Essential Skills Teacher Dashboard in 2017 using JavaScript, jQuery, Bootstrap, Ajax, PHP, JSON, AWS, and SimpleDB. This generation replaced the earlier one-page dashboard with a more conventional teacher-management interface for assignments, student/class management, reporting, charts, notifications, and school administration. It also briefly supported a parent-facing calendar and marks workflow, where teachers could create class-wide events and parents could log into a separate site to see dated messages, completed tests or assignments, and related marks.

sections.title: 2017 Dashboard Redesign
paragraphs: This was the post-one-page, pre-React generation of the Essential Skills Teacher Dashboard.
After reviewing competing products and current interface trends, I rebuilt the dashboard around a more conventional and familiar teacher-management experience.

sections.title: Solo Development
paragraphs: I designed and implemented this dashboard myself.
The broader requirements came from the real operational needs of teachers, Customer Service, management, and the existing Essential Skills platform.

sections.title: Technology Stack
paragraphs: The dashboard used a traditional web stack centered on JavaScript and jQuery rather than a frontend framework.

sections.title: More Conventional Teacher UI
paragraphs: The earlier Version 6 dashboard had used a one-page progressive-context workflow.
This redesign moved back toward a more conventional dashboard structure that ownership and users found easier to understand.

sections.title: Assignments
paragraphs: Teachers could create and manage assignments for students, groups, and classes.
Assignments integrated with the broader Essential Skills student platform and reporting systems.

sections.title: Student and Class Management
paragraphs: The dashboard provided the teacher-facing workflows needed to manage classes and students.
It remained part of the same shared Essential Skills account, assignment, marks, and reporting ecosystem.

sections.title: Reporting
paragraphs: Teachers could view student and class progress through summary and detailed reports.
The application modernized the reporting experience while retaining access to the production marks and assignment data schools already depended on.

sections.title: Custom Charts
paragraphs: The dashboard included custom visual reporting using charts and graphical summaries.
Canvas was used for parts of the reporting and visualization layer.

sections.title: Notifications
paragraphs: The dashboard surfaced important student activity and completion information so teachers could quickly identify work requiring attention.

sections.title: Teacher Calendar Events
paragraphs: This generation briefly included a teacher-created calendar/event system.
Teachers could enter class-wide events such as PA days or other group messages.

sections.title: Separate Parent Login
paragraphs: Parents accessed this information through a separate Parent Login site rather than through the Teacher Dashboard itself.
Student records carried parent email information so the parent-facing site could associate a parent with the correct child.

sections.title: Parent Calendar and Marks View
paragraphs: The parent calendar acted as a dated view of activity related to the child.
Entries represented either teacher/class messages or marks generated when the student completed tests and assignments.
items: Links to view the related marks

sections.title: Calendar as a Progress Timeline
paragraphs: The parent-facing calendar was therefore more than a conventional event calendar.
It combined teacher-created class events with a chronological view of the child's completed schoolwork and marks.

sections.title: Short-Lived Parent Feature
paragraphs: The parent calendar/login concept appears to have been abandoned relatively quickly.
It was discontinued before the later Home User subscription platform was created.

sections.title: Not Part of Home User
paragraphs: The later Home User Subscription & Parent Platform did not inherit this calendar feature.
The absence of calendar code in Home User reflects that the concept had already been dropped rather than being removed from Home User later.

sections.title: Relationship to the React Dashboard
paragraphs: This 2017 dashboard remained the primary teacher administration generation until I replaced it with the React Teacher Dashboard in 2019.
The React version retained and expanded the core teacher-management and reporting capabilities but did not continue the earlier parent-calendar concept.

sections.title: Dashboard Lineage
paragraphs: This generation sits between the earlier Version 6 one-page dashboard and the later 2019 React dashboard.

featured.description: Redesigned and built the 2017 teacher administration and reporting dashboard, including a short-lived parent-facing calendar and marks workflow.

historicalNotes: The legacy card was titled 'Teacher Assignment and Reporting App (2017)'.
The legacy description states that Jamie reconstructed the Teacher Dashboard after analyzing competitor trends in order to modernize its interface and user experience.
This is the post-one-page, pre-React Teacher Dashboard generation.
The primary stack was jQuery, Bootstrap, Ajax, PHP, JSON, AWS, and SimpleDB.
The broader Teacher Management & Reporting Systems profile already documents this generation as a more conventional redesign after the one-page Version 6 dashboard.
A newly recovered feature was a teacher-created calendar/event system connected to a separate Parent Login site.
Teachers created class-wide events such as PA days.
Student records included parent email information used by the separate Parent Login.
Parents could see dated teacher messages/events and dates when their child completed tests or assignments.
Parents could click completed work entries to view the associated marks.
The calendar represented either a teacher/class message or a marks-related completion event on a particular date.
The parent calendar/login feature was abandoned before the later Home User Subscription & Parent Platform was created.
The later Home User product therefore never contained this calendar feature.
Do not describe the calendar as having been removed from Home User.
The 2019 React Teacher Dashboard replaced this 2017 dashboard and did not continue the parent-calendar concept.
The exact font visible in surviving screenshots is not remembered and should not be treated as a stable design characteristic.
